column1: # Book 4 second-round read (Fable, 2026-10-30): every line read against the Latin. No changes.
# 4.1067 servare is under the nec of 1066; "and so lay up" could read as a thing one ought to do.
# 4.1141 proprio = love that is one's own and secure, opposed to adverso in 1142; "true" suggested sincerity.
# 4.1158 adflictentur is the mockers' reason about the others; the English had stated it as fact with an unclear "they".

column2: nor lay up for yourself care and certain pain;
